prompt.context_jp: 経理部の朝___、いつもよりわずかに張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 経理部の朝___、いつもよりわずかに張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames 'the morning in accounting' as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: は sets 'the morning in accounting' as the known topic the narrator will comment on (it felt tense). The reader already expects a scene-setting line.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would announce the morning as newly spotted information, which clashes with this calm scene-setting opening. を doesn't fit — the morning isn't being acted on.

contrast_examples.en: As for the accounting dept's morning, it's quiet (topic).
Oh, morning came! (new information with が)

prompt.context_jp: 新発田部長の明るい声___、その空気を軽く払った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 新発田部長の明るい声___、その空気を軽く払った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the manager's voice as the new element that broke the tension.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the bright voice as fresh information — something new that suddenly cuts into the tense scene and acts on the atmosphere.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the voice as an already-established topic, flattening the sudden-event feeling. に doesn't mark a subject here.

contrast_examples.en: As for that door, it's heavy (topic, は).

prompt.context_jp: 麻吹の席___、沙名子のちょうど隣に用意されている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 麻吹の席___、沙名子のちょうど隣に用意されている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Mabuki's seat as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: は presents 'Mabuki's seat' as the topic — the narrator comments on where it is, assuming the seat is contextually given.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would announce the seat as brand-new information, which is odd when the sentence is explaining its location. を doesn't fit a stative description.

prompt.context_jp: 今 経理部で主任以上なの___ 新発田部長と 田倉さんしかいないので
prompt.prompt_jp: 今 経理部で主任以上なの___ 新発田部長と 田倉さんしかいないので
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits an exhaustive 'only X and Y' identification.

feedback.correct_en: が is used for exhaustive listing: 'the ones who are supervisors or above are ONLY Manager Niihata and Takura — no one else.' The identifying/limiting function needs が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a loose topic comment and loses the 'only these two' punch. も (also) contradicts the 'only' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: The one who can go is only me (exhaustive, が).
As for me, I can't go (topic contrast, は).

prompt.context_jp: 森若さん あなた___決まりなら 無条件に従うの？
prompt.prompt_jp: 森若さん あなた___決まりなら 無条件に従うの？
prompt.prompt_en: Mabuki is challenging Moriwaka personally — pick the particle that singles her out contrastively.

feedback.correct_en: は picks out 'you (as opposed to others)' — contrastive topic. Mabuki is pointedly asking whether YOU personally would blindly obey.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'you' new information being identified, which clashes with a direct accusatory address. も (also) weakens the pointed contrast.

prompt.context_jp: 改革___経理部の仕事では ありませんので
prompt.prompt_jp: 改革___経理部の仕事では ありませんので
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle framing 'reform' as the topic Mabuki raised.

feedback.correct_en: は picks up 改革 (which Mabuki just introduced) as the topic and comments: 'as for reform — not accounting's job.' It also carries a contrastive brush-off tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly introduce 'reform' as if first mentioning it, but the word is already on the table from Mabuki's previous line. に doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: それは僕の仕事じゃない。

prompt.context_jp: 並んだ数字を追ううち、彼女の眉___かすかに寄せられる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 並んだ数字を追ううち、彼女の眉___かすかに寄せられる。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for the subject of a subtle observed change.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the eyebrows as the subject of a small, observed action — a cinematic moment the narrator notices.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame her brows as a known topic for general comment, losing the fleeting-moment feel. も (also) implies something else was furrowed first.

prompt.context_jp: 制服の着用___強制ではありません 希望者のみです
prompt.prompt_jp: 制服の着用___強制ではありません
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle introducing 'wearing a uniform' as the topic being defined.

feedback.correct_en: は presents 'wearing the uniform' as the topic and makes a general policy statement about it — the standard pattern for rule descriptions.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly identify 'uniform-wearing' as a specific item, which doesn't match a general policy explanation. を can't mark the subject of ではありません.

contrast_examples.jp: 参加が必要なのは新人だけ。
contrast_examples.en: The ones for whom participation is required are only new hires (が, exhaustive).

prompt.context_jp: おとなしく ルールを守ってる側___損をして ごねてルールを破る側___得をする
prompt.prompt_jp: ルールを守ってる側___損をして、ルールを破る側___得をする
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particles that set up a direct contrast between two sides.

feedback.correct_en: Double は creates the classic 'A は X, B は Y' contrastive structure: the rule-followers lose, the rule-breakers gain. The two sides are explicitly set against each other.
feedback.incorrect_en: Double が would be used to identify who specifically does an action, not to contrast two groups' fates. を doesn't fit as a subject marker.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄は背が高いが、弟は低い。
contrast_examples.en: The older brother is tall, but the younger is short (は...は contrast).

prompt.context_jp: その時、部内の端末に一斉に通知音___鳴り響いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部内の端末に一斉に通知音___鳴り響いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking the sudden new sound.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the notification sound as new, surprising information bursting into the scene — the classic 'sudden event' pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly treat 通知音 as a pre-established topic. を doesn't match the intransitive 鳴り響く.

prompt.context_jp: 自分のことより 好きな人___ 出来ちゃったってことでしょ？
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分のことより 好きな人___ 出来ちゃったってことでしょ？
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for a newly-appearing 'someone you like'.

feedback.correct_en: が marks 'someone-you-like' as a new entity that came into existence (出来る). 'X ができる' is a standard が pattern — spotting that something newly exists.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose this person is already a known topic, but Mizuki is diagnosing a NEW development. を can't mark the subject of 出来る.

contrast_examples.en: I got a girlfriend (newly exists, が).
My girlfriend is kind (established topic, は).

prompt.context_jp: 森若「日常業務は戦いの場じゃありません」麻吹「私___常に戦いだと思ってます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___常に戦いだと思ってます
prompt.prompt_en: Mabuki is distinguishing her view from Moriwaka's. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は is contrastive: 'YOU may not think so, but I personally see everything as a battle.' It sets her stance against Moriwaka's.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make '私' new information being identified as the one who thinks so, which isn't the point. も (also) wrongly implies agreement.

contrast_examples.en: I don't think so (contrastive with others, は).

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子は自席で、山田が置いていった伝票___目を落とした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 山田が置いていった伝票___目を落とした
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: her eyes fell ONTO the voucher.

feedback.correct_en: 目を落とす takes に for the target — her gaze landed ON the voucher. The direct object slot (を) is already taken by 目.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would duplicate the direct-object role already filled by 目を. が doesn't fit as a locative/target marker here.

contrast_examples.en: Drop one's eyes onto a letter (に target).

prompt.context_jp: 必要なときは 私か田倉さん___言っていただければ
prompt.prompt_jp: 必要なときは 私か田倉さん___言っていただければ
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle meaning 'tell TO me or Takura'.

feedback.correct_en: に marks the recipient — the person being spoken to. 言う takes に for the addressee.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would turn the person into the thing being said, which is nonsensical. で marks location/means, not an addressee.

prompt.context_jp: 気がつけば足は勝手に動き、沙名子は目の前の道___全力で駆け出していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子は目の前の道___全力で駆け出していた
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: she dashed along/through the road.

feedback.correct_en: を with motion verbs marks the path traversed — she ran ALONG the road. 駆け出す/走る/歩く take を for 'through/along'.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mean 'ran TO the road' (destination), which doesn't fit a sprint down it. で (location of action) is possible but less natural for a traversed path.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子は静かに立ち上がり、山田を廊下へ呼び出した。「これは… 経費で___！」
prompt.prompt_jp: これは… 経費で___！
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the signature catchphrase: 'This... can't be expensed!'

feedback.correct_en: 経費で落ちる is the set accounting idiom — 'to be allowed as an expense / to pass as expensable.' Negated: 落ちません = 'won't go through as an expense.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 降りる (come down) and 通る (pass) don't collocate with 経費 in this idiomatic sense; they'd sound off to Japanese ears.

contrast_examples.jp: この飲み会は経費で落ちる？
contrast_examples.en: Can this drinking party be expensed?

prompt.context_jp: 「よっ！ 名___体を表す」
prompt.prompt_jp: 名___体を表す
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the Japanese proverb: 'The name tells the person.'

feedback.correct_en: 名は体を表す is a fixed proverb meaning 'the name represents the person/thing.' The particle slot is locked as は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が or を would break the set form. Proverbs don't accept substitutions.

contrast_examples.en: A name shows the nature (set proverb).
Birds of a feather flock together (another は proverb).

prompt.context_jp: フッ… "___神に祟りなし" ってことですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: ___神に祟りなし
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb: 'A god untouched won't curse you' (let sleeping dogs lie).

feedback.correct_en: 触らぬ神に祟りなし — 'a god you don't touch won't curse you' — is the fixed form Mabuki is quoting back sarcastically.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見ぬ and 知らぬ exist in other proverbs (見ぬが花, 知らぬが仏) but don't fit this specific set phrase.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子は反射的に___を下げ、決まりごとを一つずつ確認するように書類を受け取った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子は反射的に___を下げた
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in: she reflexively lowered her ___ (= bowed).

feedback.correct_en: 頭を下げる is the standard collocation for 'to bow / to lower one's head' as a gesture of politeness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 顔を下げる and 目を下げる aren't idiomatic; 目を落とす (drop one's eyes) uses 落とす, not 下げる.

prompt.context_jp: 教育が___なくても しかたないわ
prompt.prompt_jp: 教育が___なくても しかたないわ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in: 'even if her training hasn't fully reached her'.

feedback.correct_en: 行き届く = 'to be thoroughgoing / to reach every corner.' 教育が行き届く is a set collocation for 'training being thorough.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 終わる (end) and 届ける (deliver, transitive) don't carry the 'thoroughness' nuance; 届ける wouldn't match 教育が either.

contrast_examples.jp: 掃除が行き届いている。

prompt.context_jp: 淡々とした口調の一言一言に、自分への確信が___いる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分への確信が___いる
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb: '(confidence) seeps through her words'.

feedback.correct_en: 滲む (nijimu) = 'to seep/bleed through' — used metaphorically for an emotion or quality that quietly permeates speech or expression.
feedback.incorrect_en: 流れる (flow) and 広がる (spread) are too dynamic/physical; they lose the subtle 'quietly imbued' feeling.

contrast_examples.en: Tears well up in one's eyes.

prompt.context_jp: 追及しないほうが いいこともあるということです。「___ないほうがいい」
prompt.prompt_jp: 追及___ないほうが いいこともある
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb stem meaning 'to press/pursue (an issue)'.

feedback.correct_en: 追及 is a する-verb noun; 追及する → 追及しない. The ない-form is 追及しない.
feedback.incorrect_en: 追及い / 追及れ aren't valid conjugations — this is a noun+する compound, not an ichidan or godan verb.

prompt.context_jp: Mabuki is scolding Moriwaka for blindly following rules.
prompt.prompt_en: Which option sounds more natural as Mabuki's challenging line?

choices.text: 森若さん、あなたは決まりなら無条件に従うの？
森若さん、あなたが決まりなら無条件に従うの？

feedback.correct_en: は singles out 'you' contrastively — the pointed, accusatory address needed here. This matches the chapter's actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn the question into 'who it is that follows rules' (identifying), which doesn't fit a direct personal challenge.

contrast_examples.en: What do YOU think? (personal address, は)

prompt.context_jp: Yamada is a cheerful sales rep speaking casually to Moriwaka in the hallway.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural for Yamada's casual, youthful speech?

choices.text: ほっておけないっす 一緒にいたいです
放置することができません 共にいることを望みます

feedback.correct_en: 〜っす is a casual-polite spoken contraction used by young men like Yamada; combined with simple vocabulary it matches his breezy sincerity.
feedback.incorrect_en: The B version uses stiff written/formal vocabulary (放置する, 共に, 望む) that would sound bizarre as spoken flirtation from a sales guy.

contrast_examples.jp: 非常に憂慮すべき事態です。
contrast_examples.en: This is a highly concerning situation (stiff written register).

prompt.context_jp: Mabuki is introducing herself to her new coworker on her first day.
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting is more natural for a formal workplace self-introduction?

choices.text: はい よろしくお願いいたします
うん よろしく頼むね

feedback.correct_en: よろしくお願いいたします is the standard polite workplace self-introduction phrase, matching Mabuki's crisp, formal register.
feedback.incorrect_en: よろしく頼むね is casual and used downward (to subordinates/friends) — inappropriate when meeting a new colleague for the first time.

contrast_examples.jp: よろしくお願いいたします。
contrast_examples.en: Pleased to work with you (formal workplace).

prompt.context_jp: Mabuki criticizes printing out vouchers that could be handled digitally.
prompt.prompt_en: Which rhetorical complaint sounds more natural in Mabuki's assertive style?

choices.text: システムだけで処理できるものを ムダじゃないですか？
システムだけで処理することが可能であるのに 無駄ではないでしょうか？

feedback.correct_en: The A version uses natural spoken rhythm (〜ものを, ムダじゃないですか) that conveys frustration directly — matching her sharp conversational style.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatically fine but reads like a written report; it's over-formal and loses the pointed, in-the-moment challenge.

contrast_examples.jp: できるのに、やらないの？
contrast_examples.en: You could, but you don't? (spoken challenge)

contrast_examples.jp: 実施可能であるにもかかわらず、未実施である。

prompt.context_jp: Sanako suddenly sprints away from Yamada after his confession.
prompt.prompt_en: Which inner exclamation sounds more natural for Sanako's shocked realization mid-sprint?

choices.text: 私 走ってる！ すごく走ってる！
私は走っている。非常に走っている。

feedback.correct_en: Dropped particles, short bursts, and すごく capture a breathless, surprised interior monologue — exactly her panicked moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: The B version uses full-form 走っている and 非常に (written/formal 'extremely'), making it sound like a lab report rather than a startled inner voice.

contrast_examples.en: Crap, I won't make it! (natural inner voice)
This is deeply regrettable (stiff written tone).
